intent_en: To demonstrate that the reduction in road casualties in Britain has primarily benefited car drivers, while cyclists have not experienced similar safety improvements and continue to face significant danger.
previous_intent: To illustrate that the significant reduction in road casualties in Britain over the last decade has primarily benefited car drivers, while cyclists have not seen similar safety improvements and continue to face significant danger.
narration_support: the bulk of this safety benefit has been felt by people in cars. Cyclists face nearly as much danger.
chart_support: Line chart showing the index of people killed or injured on British roads from 2007 to 2016, where the trend for car drivers decreases significantly while the trend for cyclists increases.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly states that safety benefits are mostly for car drivers and cyclists face similar danger. The chart visualizes this divergence: the green line (car drivers) drops from ~145 to ~60, while the blue line (cyclists) rises from ~85 to ~110, confirming the disparity.
